I'm pleased with the execution on a lot of the plays. I think we're in the right direction. We just want to get it going faster than what it is right now. >> When you have a guy like AJ Cole who has a Howard sir at the end of his like is it more of a just leave him alone and let him do what he's doing or is there ways that you can even help him when he's at such an elite level? >> Yeah, you hope you can from a protection standpoint more than anything else. You want to have a clean pocket for him just like a quarterback, you know, the cleaner his pocket is the more accurate he can be and I think with AJ it's the same thing, you know, you just got to keep things as as space free as possible. We want to have him to have space to operate in right there where he's able to hit his targets and everything but you know, I would think you would tell he would tell you that probably his last two games haven't been up to his standard and I you know, he'll he'll he'll get it going. I really did. And we had to make a a quick decision. And uh that's the decision we made. And that's when we said we can't lose the the pain, the decision, the lessons that we learned from what happened, right? You have to keep the the lessons that you learned from failure. And that that's a reminder we said we left out, right? Don't blame it on the committee. We didn't do what it takes to make it into the playoffs. And so we use that as a reminder to take advantage of the now though, right? I think there's this there's a misconception that we're talking about we want to leave no doubt for the season and all this. Yeah. But that's a reflection of leaving no doubt with what you have in front of you. And so in our building, we use it as a mentality to take advantage of right now, what you have um this game, this minute um and today. >> The process, baby, it's undefeated. the process. If you can focus on it and master it, the outcomes will come your way. AJ has the last question for you, coach. >> Yeah, Marcus, are you like are you having fun? Are you enjoying being the Notre Dame head football coach? We we had Nick Sabin on a little bit ago and he said he was he realized he was in a hurry for 50 years. He didn't realize until he got done. And he said he never truly got to enjoy things because it was always next. Here we go. I'm playing golf. I got to go call some recruits. Everything. And I can understand. You are always curating like what's it like? Are you having fun? I guess are you having fun? And also like I would imagine now it's a lot more fun than it was when you first showed up. >> Yeah, there's there's I don't know that there's anything um very probably very few things that bring me more joy than making an impact on the young people you get a chance to to be around every day, right? When you see them go to the NFL. When you see like that's the fun, right? And that's that that that's the greatest joy of this position is that you get a chance to impact young people every day. And that's where I get my fulfillment. It has nothing to do with wins. Um it it it does have to do with wins because when you see their face, when you see those guys um enjoying the fruits of victory, that that brings a lot of joy. Um and so that's what I would tell you, AJ. Yeah, there's a lot of things that this position um um really has and entails and you have to do, but the joy comes from the players. The joy comes from seeing others have success. >> Well, we take a lot of joy in seeing this Golden Dome fly around. Good luck tomorrow against these Cougs. Hey, there's a they've been lining up for game day since Tuesday night. I I mean, there's an anticipation and obviously when Notre Dame comes to town, it is a big game for everybody. title: Nick Saban Breaks Down The BIGGEST Games In Week 7 Of College Football
text: We are here with Nata Kelly Papinga or the Kelly Papawski. We are here with Kapawski. We are here with the greatest college football coach of all time, Nick Saban. >> Yeah, coach. >> Coach, you had documentary released about you last week. How do you feel now that everybody knows everything about you? >> Uh really no different. You know, we haven't had a chance to, you know, see the whole thing yet. We've been a little busy, but um got a lot of good comments about it. I'm glad people enjoyed it. I hope they learn something. You know, it's really about being a tribute to all the people who contributed to the success and giving them an opportunity to express themselves in terms of their experience. And hopefully this will help, you know, somebody out there have a better chance to be successful. >> And that take was brought to you by DoorDash. The race there [laughter] is Foxy put that up immediately upon you start talking. We apologize, but we also want to let people know don't fan for free. Right now whenever you DoorDash on Saturdays, you could potentially be a big time winner. Maybe enough money for a house, maybe a car, maybe a truck, maybe groceries for a year. Shout out to DoorDash. Shout out to you Saban. I know you continue to say this is for um like everybody to be a part of the story, everybody be a part of the story. Me and the lads have watched I've watched 75% of it. I have not finished it yet. I will get to it by the end of this weekend. There's a couple guys back in the Thunderdome who have watched 100% of it. >> We finished it this morning as everyone watching it together. >> Okay, so coach you need to know you're you're a legend, dude. Just you're your competitive spirit, your drive for lifting others, your misery too in the biggest moments and being able to continue to draw from that. It's just you're a special story. We just told Ryan Smith this who became a billionaire when he was 41. Now he's 49. He owns two teams and a bunch of other businesses as well. He's a great American dream story. You, just a football guy from West Virginia. And what we're learning about you, thank you for existing, dude. Actually, I hope you understand that that's coming out of this documentary as well, cuz a lot of people are saying, "Thank god for that hillbilly from West Virginia getting into ball and doing his thing." We're very lucky for you, actually. >> But you know, the one thing that I hope people can see and understand is you know, we're so transactional, you know, in sports cuz everything's about winning and losing. And the thing about being a little more transformational, caring about the players, players don't care what you know until they know what you care. Being tough on them, tough love, getting them to do the things that are going to help them be successful in the future. We just did a little different way, you know, trying to be a leader that they could emulate. And you know, wanted them to know we were trying to help them be successful for their benefit, not our benefit. And we had a vision for what they could do and try to lead them and help them and inspire them to do it. And you know, I think it was a little different approach, but it worked well for us. And I just love all the cast of characters who contributed to it. >> Yeah, I think you did a great job, coach. You should be incredibly proud of yourself. Now, college football has changed mightily. How old are you? >> I'm going to be 75 Halloween. >> There you go. >> Damn, Halloween's your birthday? Sick. >> Halloween, baby. >> Trick or treat, mama don't know which. >> [laughter] >> We love mama. We appreciate mama for that, but I guess she was wondering that. I mean, you just being a goblin, you know, going into all these different college football stadiums and dominating people. Halloween birthday is spectacular. But you're 75. And a lot of people say that the changing of college football is what forced you to retire. But I think becoming a seven-time national champion, being considered the greatest of all time, and in your 70s, and not really ever living your life potentially fell into the decision as well with Miss Terry. But with how fast and how rapid college football has changed, where do you kind of sit on that now that you're media looking in at it? And I know it's hard not to take your coaching hat off, but if you were to look at it and then now hearing about the 2014 playoff, what do you think about where college football is, where it was when you retired, and where this has been a lot of change very quickly, I think, to a sport that has a lot of tradition. The 2014 playoff is the most recent one. How do you feel about it as a guy who's dedicated your life to the sport? >> Well, first of all, I really didn't retire because college football was changing. Um, you know, we always wanted to help players be more successful in life. That became a little more difficult with NIL and players getting paid, which I think they deserved and um and I was happy for them to be able to do it. It just changed, you know, the whole game in terms of transfer portal, um guys how much they're getting paid, how does that affect their ability to work on the things they need to do to develop personally, academically, and athletically. I think those are all questions that we want to make sure that in college we keep education first and development first and make the quality of life better and find a balance in all that and a competitive balance in all that. But, the 2014 playoff is, you know, my only concern about the 2014 playoff is I understand the more teams you get involved, the more interest it creates and more opportunity, the more hope that it creates for, you know, players. But, the one thing that I am concerned about because we played 15 games three or four times and that was a lot of games for college players. Now, we're talking about in a 2014 playoff you could play five more games um and the 12 games and what happens at championship games and how we eliminate those and uh I just get a little concerned about um how much is too much when it comes to how many games a college player plays. >> Okay, so you're you're not for the 24 team playoff necessarily. >> Uh I would be for 16. I think that would be a good compromise. Um I would be for keeping conference championship games as maybe a play-in to the 16, which now you'd have 20 teams that had hope. But um I don't think there's much support for that. I don't think anybody really likes that. So >> Yeah, well I don't think there's there's not necessarily a lot of people that love the 24 team. We are finding things to love about the 24 team. I don't think any of us are saying, "Yep, this is the right decision." But I think it is reality. And the people that are making this decision, the CFP, which are what commissioners and ADs and all this type of stuff, there has to be a reason that they would like it. And what we've been trying to figure out is what is the exact reason if you were to get to the bottom of it because it doesn't feel like anybody's out here pounding the drum for it. And hope is certainly what it is, but it's also like to keep the sport going how it is for a lot of these places. For these boosters, if your team doesn't have success, I don't think the money keeps coming in. And I think that is a realization of all these universities like, "Hey, we have to have some sort of success or we're going to potentially get cut off of this entire thing." I think that is a big drawer for this. Not saying that's right or wrong, but I do think that is a massive piece of the puzzle that isn't really being talked about. >> Yeah, I I think that uh you're 100% right and I loved your dissertation of how you explained all those things. But the bottom line is money. >> Okay. >> That's the bottom line. I mean, you you explained that universities need it because of the way we're spending more now for players and there's still a cost to having Olympic sports, which are important I think to be able to keep and give people opportunities to compete. Um and how do we do that? Um but I think we also have to look at some kind of budget that we can have so that everybody kind of is competing at the same level and everybody can plan on how much are we going to spend here? And I want players to make money and I want them to have name, image, likeness opportunities, but I think we have to put some kind of budget on it so people can operate. Every business has a budget. I don't know how any business survives if you don't have a budget. So, why wouldn't we need that in college athletics? >> Yeah, in the NFL, obviously easy to say that they have it figured out and they are professional football, which is what college football has become. So, there's always the comparison to that. And then FCS, I believe they've had a 2014 playoff since like 2013 or something like that. So, they've done it before and I'm not saying that it's the exact same as FBS football, but it has happened before. The amount of games are worrisome, but with the interest and the ratings and everything that college football is, we just got to keep that going forward and I hope no decision, including a 2014 playoff one, stops that at all cuz there's so much growth for college football right now. It's such a special sport. We got kids camping out to be a part of a pregame show for the sport. That's how special the sport is. We can never tamper with that, I think. >> I'm 100% in agreement with you. I don't think people realize how much passion there is and how many opportunities are created by college athletics and college sports and we have to keep it sacred in terms of how we approach it in the future. >> Okay, let's talk about college football and sacred, shall we? I think they will be tested by BYU. I think BYU has a challenging defense. They're very aggressive in terms of how they pressure the quarterback and you know, can Notre Dame run the ball against them? Can they handle their odd front which they pressure a lot out, mostly simulated. They play a lot of man-to-man so they got to beat man coverage. How good is Notre Dame skill players outside? I do think that he has improved as a passer and is a more complete player this year than he was a year ago and I think BYU is a pretty good football team. >> Yeah, I think they're a pretty good football team and I think this energy could propel them. Everybody's expecting Notre Dame to have a great day including sportsbooks. Double-digit favorite coming out here. Hello, we are here for real. Basketball has been getting the number one recruit the last couple years here out of BYU. Football team has been close to winning the Big 12 to get into the dance, do their thing. If they beat Notre Dame on primetime, big one, be a gigantic for the entire program. title: LIVE: HC Dan Quinn Speaks To The Media After Practice | Washington Commanders
text: All right, you guys ready to roll? Okay, first off, I thought I was impressed by our team's practice uh this week. I thought the overall energy vibe to prep to practice and to prepare uh speaks to the locker room speaks to the leadership. We had a Friday style practice today. Um and we'll head to San Francisco tonight. And uh you know, like as a whole team, man, like we're very excited for this opportunity. And uh know you may ask some questions regarding some injuries. So I will uh give you four that will rule out today and uh those four will be Bill, Javvante, Charles and Marcus and uh outside of those four um everyone's traveling and I'll have you know all the way till Monday this week to you know make decisions as far as playing not but you know to get everybody back in and going was a big deal for us and those four um won't make the trip. So and expect uh some updates on Monday. >> Um going back to what you saw this week, at what point do you know the page has been turned and what do you see that tells you that? >> Yeah, I would say the extra day this week probably helped. Um I noticed it where it turned, John, I would say it's at practice on Thursday. That was our first practice day of the weekend. So in meetings, you're teaching, you're going through, you're installing, you're getting ready, but it was at practice and uh we really, you know, made a big push on our execution. I love the team's fight. Could the execution and the fight could they sync up? And seeing that at practice, uh that was a sign, you know, and that's what I was looking for honestly as I went out to practice that was good to see. And then you you know you said you make the decisions Monday, but with um Bill out, the likelihood for Jeremy and what kind of role could he have? >> Yeah, like I said, we'll get to the final things by Monday, but um like this is a one of our most professional um ball players on off what he can bring. And so as we get to uh Monday, uh he's had a very good week and we'll decide from there. >> It's okay. um with Bill kind of what is are you able to say kind of what what he's facing long term? >> Sure. He had a um a reinjury of his groin and so um that's harder you know on the same injury and so um we're do you know work really hard to get him back but uh you know that that was same groin injury. I repeat that with >> with that room in general. I know you talked about sort of the the flux of the group um but with Rashad White what have you seen from him already this season? What do you need to see from him? Especially, you know, with Bill being out. >> Sure. A new um like natural athlete catching, you know, out of the back field to going. What I see is like these glide and he can make a cut and make big plays on that. So, uh having Ek back here too, there's, you know, like his explosiveness in the passing game, you know, is a big deal. So, having, you know, some combination of the guys, I think that's, you know, what we'll lean on most right now. Hey coach, you talked a little bit earlier during the week about just the execution ending critical plays. Y in practice this week. What have you seen as far as the execution on both sides of the ball? >> Yep. I think it starts first um Donna, this was the fewest penalties in a week and uh you know had an extra person, but to see that part uh come together um more significant. and I felt the speed um very few repeats, you know, in a play. Let's not let's hit that again. So, those were some of the topics that I wanted to see, you know, on our core concepts. Could we absolutely go nail those? And so, on the first part of the week, lots of first and second down, then we worked into the third down and and then even today as like a big red zone emphasis. So, I wanted to see each of the days, could we execute in the next phase? And so like for us, we threw a good week and that's why we're excited for the opportunity. >> And looking at the 49ers on offense, they really do a good job with their explosive plays. And when you look at your defensive side of the ball, what have you drilled this week as far as making sure that that is really cleaned up? >> Yeah, that has to be the case. Um, they've got an excellent point differential, San Fran. Like they haven't allowed a lot of big plays. They've created some. And so knowing where your eyes are, you know, there's a lot of shift motion that can go on with the offense. And then knowing, you know, where the premium big plays come from, you know, wide receiver, tight end, running back, and making sure on the specific calls, how you're guarding it, what you're doing, and uh then I think the second plays, you know, that you know, pretty outside the pocket on the scramles, those are big ones, too. Donna, >> hey, coach. Um, this has been a week and so what have you seen from Jaden? I know you, you know, from the three years and dealing with the injuries and just how he's dealt with this week and addressing his teammates. What have you seen from him? >> Yeah, I think um there's a maturity about him that um definitely comes through. Candy, that's number one. Um his relentless nature to prepare and dig in is always evident, but I also know like man, he's got a lot of fight in him. And sometimes those get demonstrated in the hardest moments as well, whether that's coming back from an injury or um difficult moment, all of that. And so he knows it goes with the position, but I'd also say um there's been a lot of growth this whole season of 2026 coming back from an injury, new offense, um leading, you know, like there's an elevated presence about him. It's very easy to see and uh I noticed it. >> And um 49ers on Monday night. What is something you What are the things you must see from your team on Monday night? >> Yeah, we must see um the play style that we like. We must, you know, in all three phases. And then the next thing is I'm we must see like the execution of our systems. And that doesn't mean every play is perfect, but it does mean um right spot, right location, right hit, all of those to go. Uh both these teams are physical and San Francisco's proven, you know, not to be a team that beats themsel. And so I think the execution for us, that's that's the at the top of the pile. And we need to be, you know, certainly be able to play manageable third downs on both sides. I think that's going to be a big factor in the game. Um, with Charles and Javvante being out, obviously you're going to need some guys to step up in that edge rusher room. Um, what sort of progressions have you seen from Joshua Joseph as as a rookie so far? >> Yeah, I uh I have seen and like when you're growing, there's kind of like the ups and downs to where it goes. I'm not talking about just from a game performance, but the practice. And so to see him, and I really felt that this week, more plays, more opportunities, and uh I don't if that's comfort in the system, but I would say comfort in knowing you can get it done and doing it. And so um I've always felt his length, you know, as an edge setter, but now see him bending, see him going. Um and like I said, he'll have some more snaps, too. >> Morning, Dan. Good morning. Um you all got some explosive plays last week, particularly on the ground with Jaden, but The 49ers, I think, allowed a third least amount of explosive plays. So, two-part. One, what did you like about the ability to get your explosive plays last week? What does San Francisco do that you can see that limits other teams from being able to get it on? >> Yep. I'll start backwards if that's okay. Um, starting with San Francisco. So, I think with Ron and their defense, um, I see a good tackling team, you know, that like, you know, sprints to go and there's a completion, you see the second, third guy get there quickly. And for us, that's, you know, one example of one of the things that I see from them. Uh, and then for us, they can come in a number of different ways. It doesn't mean it's, you know, like sometimes we think explosive or just like a deep ball, but the explosive means it could be catch and run. It could be, you know, a seam. And so when the moments are there for us to deliver on those, we got to go hit them. And that could mean Jaden legs and throwing or and scramble to go. But I like the plan that the guys put together for the week. You don't chase them, but you do have to hunt them. All right. What is the difference? Well, when the moments are there in this system, man, like there it is. That's the one to go get it. If it's not, like you get to the next progression, you get to the next play. And so I'm looking forward to to seeing us execute. >> Um coach, this is a prime time stretch for you guys. Next four or five on prime time with that by week in the middle. Um Terry said yesterday it's a opportunity for this team to be able to show out in front of a national audience. How do you look at some of these bigger national stage games? >> Yeah, they're um it is fun to have a you know national game where um you know like on for instance this one the only game you know that's playing and so for people to see that and know um it's a big deal for us. Um but quite honestly like just in this week that's all the focus that that's there for us into this one and uh it's going to be a hell of a battle and uh we're looking forward to the out. >> Thanks. >> All right. Thanks everybody. We'll see you there. >> Ask a question.
